SLA Language Reference > Structs and Enums

Structs and Enums

This page introduces how aggregate types are declared: named-field structs, tuple-like structs, newtypes, generic structs, enums with payloads, and static and dynamic dispatch via trait/impl/dyn. After reading this page, you can choose a suitable aggregate form for business data and organize its methods.

Named structs

// demos/rosetta/05_struct/main.sla
struct Point {
    x: i32,
    y: i32,
}

fn create_point(x: i32, y: i32) -> Point {
    Point { x: x, y: y }
}

Fields are accessed with .; a struct literal must list all fields (or use the ..base update syntax, see the Pattern Matching page).

Tuple-like structs and newtypes

Fields are accessed by position: .0/.1/…. The single-field form is the newtype pattern:

// demos/rosetta/36_tuple_struct / 37_newtype
struct Color(u8, u8, u8);
struct UserId(u32);

let color = Color(2, 4, 8);
let c0 = color.0 as i32;

let user = UserId(42);
println("{}", user.0);

Enums and payloads

enum supports three forms: variants without payloads, named-field variants, and tuple-like variants, seen in demos 06 and 43 respectively:

enum Message {
    Quit,
    Move { x: i32, y: i32 },
}

enum Shape {
    Circle(i32),
    Square(i32),
}

// 构造：Message::Move { x: 10, y: 20 }、Shape::Square(6)
NoteSLA also has the union keyword for union types in FFI scenarios (rosetta 113_union_ffi_types); for everyday modeling, prefer enum.

Generic structs

// demos/rosetta/10_generics_monomorph/main.sla
struct OptionValue<T> {
    is_some: bool,
    value: T,
}

let opt = OptionValue<i32> { is_some: true, value: 42 };

Each combination of type arguments is monomorphized at compile time into an independent layout, at no runtime cost.

trait and impl: static dispatch

// demos/rosetta/07_trait_vtable/main.sla
trait Draw {
    fn draw(&self) -> i32;
}

impl Draw for Button {
    fn draw(&self) -> i32 {
        self.id
    }
}

dyn Trait: dynamic dispatch

dyn Trait, combined with borrowing, puts different concrete types at the same call site, and the compiler generates a vtable: 

fn render(&item: dyn Draw) -> i32 {
    item.draw()
}

let button = Button { id: 77 };
let result = render(&button);   // 77

Layout contract (TS-21, written 2026-10-29)

The memory layout of aggregate types has general rules (both backends share the same layout plan, lowering_rules.structFieldLayout), now written as follows: struct fields are laid out in declaration order, with no reordering; each field's offset is aligned to its storage alignment; all fields of a union are at offset 0. An enum's discriminant tag is an i64 at offset 0, and the payload starts at offset 8. FFI by-value struct passing and serialization may rely on this contract.
